note: _et dedit illis potestatem spirituum immundorum_ (Clementina, NVg) – and he gave them power over (genitivus objectivus) unclean spirits. Read, or rather misread, as genitivus subjectivus, the expression would mean: he made them have the power of unclean spirits.

_et quicunque non receperit vos, neque audierit sermons verstros: exeuntes foras_ (…) – and whoever has not welcomed you, nor listened to your words – (you will be) those who go out (..). This is an anacoluthon – a syntactical discontinuity; the words before and the words after the colon [:] are not syntactically linked. The Nova Vulgata does not change the sentence.

_mitto vos sicut oves in medio luporum_ – I send you like sheep to the wolves. The Latin is all but elegant. A literal rendering might be: I will send you (to be) like sheep among wolves. In classical Latin, it would be _mitto vos tamquam oves inter lupos_ (Castellion).

_nonne duo passeres asse veneunt: et unus ex illis non cadet super terram sine Patre vestro?_ (Clementina) – Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? And not one of them shall fall on the ground without your Father (Douay Version). The Clementina has the question mark [?] in the wrong place, and the Douay Version places it correctly – as does the Nova Vulgata.
